prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Transparent pixel-art PROJECTILE SPRITE for the Grove Warden tower-defense prototype. Reference is the original three-frame projectile atlas: it shows 3 repeated flight frames horizontally. Use its FIRST frame only as style reference. Output ONE SINGLE flight pose, NOT an atlas and NOT three repeated copies. EXACTLY THREE parallel arrows, a robust steel arrowhead and warm wooden shaft on each. Dark steel binding at the neck. Approximate native occupied size22x40.
All arrowheads point straight UP, aligned in a horizontal row; shafts long and slender downward with tiny feather tails, like the reference. Parallel arrows separated by thin transparent vertical gaps. They form one compact visible salvo without a physical connecting bar. Native design has about40 pixels height and the specified native width, shown enlarged in hard square nearest-neighbour pixel blocks. Simple clean 2-3-tone clusters, dark plum outlines and muted original palette. Every arrow visible from tip to tail, no clipping. There is NO bow, crossbow, cannon, building, magic effect, glowing trail, starburst or impact in this asset. No labels, numbers, borders, ground, checkerboard, backdrop or shadow. Genuine transparent alpha around the sprites, opaque pixel edges, no antialiasing, no halo. The projectile should look like ammunition actually released from the existing medieval mechanical crossbows, legible when very small. Center the single compact salvo with transparent margin.
